clue.text: Comfort very delicate thing

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'
lace is a fine, delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: Someone takes comfort in a fragile treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort given in grief or distress, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One naming each character a witch?

definitions.meaning: someone who says the letters of a word in turn
one who casts spells, a sorceress

explanation.definitionFit: A speller names letters in order, and whimsically a witch is someone who makes spells.

clue.text: Line taken after slippery customer turning up, appearing suspicious

indicators.note: taken after says the line comes after the other piece
in a down clue turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an eel is a proverbially slippery creature
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A shifty character arrives after the queue, looking suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' is a railway line (RY), not L; 'turning up' turns EEL into LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means wary or distrustful, a synonym of suspicious.

clue.text: 11, Conservative, last to gain help from the right

indicators.note: to gain says the final letter takes the reversed word before it

parts.note: David Cameron was the Conservative prime minister

indicators.note: from the right means the word is read right to left

parts.note: aid means help
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A player, a Tory, finally gaining support from the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' is Z, the last letter of the alphabet; AID reversed is DIA. The answer is the film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The American actress is a player in the acting sense, 11-across being PLAYER.

clue.text: Fear ultimately contained by animal, though bit of a chicken

indicators.note: contained by says the letter goes inside the word for animal

parts.note: a beast is an animal

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word fear

explanation.surface: A creature holds a little fear, though it is only part chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is a cut of meat from a chicken, so it is a part of the bird.

clue.text: See 23
11 appears as uncertain about range of perception

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about says the word for uncertain surrounds the other piece

parts.note: hazy means vague or uncertain
ken is one's range of knowledge or perception

explanation.surface: A player looks unsure about how much he can see.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN, as in 'beyond my ken', is a Scots word for range of knowledge. The answer is the Russian-born pianist and conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir, the concert pianist, is a player in the musical sense, 11-across being PLAYER.

clue.text: Labour finds a victorious leader in course

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the word for course

parts.note: a trail is a course or route

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of victorious

explanation.surface: Hard work finds a winning captain on the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful, arduous labour, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Points made at last by TS Eliot and he's let off

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The poet makes a final point and lets someone off the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'let off', but it is the anagram signal for TS ELIOT and HE'S LET together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiletto heels are high, sharply pointed heels, so they are points.

clue.text: From Europe, league 11

indicators.note: From says the letters are taken out of the run of words Europe, league

explanation.surface: A footballer picked from a European league.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer at 11-across, PLAYER, which defines every themed entry; this one is the Brazilian footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian footballer is one of the most famous sports players ever.

clue.text: Meat loaf, then fool

parts.note: mutton is the meat of sheep
loaf means head, from rhyming slang 'loaf of bread'

explanation.surface: A recipe for meatloaf, followed by a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat loaf' reads as one dish, but it splits: 'loaf' is British rhyming slang (loaf of bread = head), as in 'use your loaf'.
explanation.definitionFit: A muttonhead is an informal insult for a dull, stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: One competing (at golf?)

parts.note: a general word for any competitor, with the bracket nodding at Gary, the famous South African golfer of that surname

explanation.surface: Someone taking part, perhaps on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone taking part in a game is a participant of this kind; Gary of that name was a great golfer.

clue.text: Call setter revolutionary, receiving one as loyal follower

indicators.note: receiving says the reversed string takes the numeral inside it
revolutionary means turned right round, so the call and setter words together are read backwards

parts.note: to call something is to name it
gel is a setting agent, something that sets
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Calling the compiler a revolutionary, while keeping someone as a faithful disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' tempts the solver towards the crossword compiler, but here it is a jelly-like setting agent; 'revolutionary' turns the call and setter words round together before 'receiving' adds I.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a feudal vassal sworn to serve his lord, hence a loyal follower.

clue.text: Start to perform at Speakers' Corner — perhaps London's after one to provide content

indicators.note: to provide content means something goes inside as the filling of the speaking word

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech, as people do at Speakers' Corner in London's Hyde Park

indicators.note: after says the spirit follows the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
London gin is a style of dry gin, so London's suggests gin

explanation.surface: A speaker at Hyde Park begins, with London as the source of the material.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner, in London's Hyde Park, is a famous spot for open-air public speeches. 'perhaps London's' is a definition by example: London dry gin.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to start or begin something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rude guzzling starter — slow down?

parts.note: grace is said before eating, the start of a meal
less, as in lessen, suggests easing down or slowing

explanation.surface: A rude eater tucks in, then is told to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guzzling starter' is not a first course but the grace said before eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceless means lacking manners or courtesy, close to rude.

clue.text: I change nappies as 11

parts.note: I stands for the setter, whose pseudonym is Paul
a New Man is the modern man who shares childcare, such as changing nappies

explanation.surface: The setter says he changes nappies, like an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Paul, so 'I' is his name. A New Man is the 1980s British term for a man who shares housework and childcare; nappies are diapers. The answer is the American actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The American film star was a player in the acting sense, 11-across being PLAYER.

clue.text: See 3
Stooped to initial, having no initial in document

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the word for document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document

indicators.note: having no initial means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to initial a paper is to sign it

explanation.surface: Someone lowered themselves to initial a document without their initials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' is used twice: first as 'sign', then as 'first letter', so SIGN loses S to make IGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to doing something beneath one's dignity, so deigned means stooped.

clue.text: Plant at £500 a head

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A price tag of five hundred pounds apiece.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'monkey' is British slang for £500. The surface reads as a price, but 'Plant' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey nut is another name for the peanut plant and its pods.

clue.text: Territory no good party covered by imperialistic work

indicators.note: covered by says these letters go inside the name of the novel

parts.note: Kim is Kipling's novel of British India, often called imperialist
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A land where a useless party is hidden by imperialist writing.
explanation.walkthrough: KIM is Rudyard Kipling's 1901 novel set in British India.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a realm or territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Ignorant girl battling with drug

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
battling suggests war, being at war
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A naive young woman fighting a drug habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaware means not knowing, so ignorant of something.

clue.text: Dash off one's life's work

definitions.meaning: to rush away at speed, hurtle

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means rushing headlong; as a noun it is a working life or profession.

clue.text: 11 from left getting one-two round back of defence

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: round says the word for two goes around the letter

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two of something

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of defence

explanation.surface: A footballer on the left plays a one-two around the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface misleads: a 'one-two' is a quick pass, but here it is I and BRACE, with E (end of defence) inside BRACE after its B. The answer is the flamboyant pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamboyant American pianist was a player in the musical sense, 11-across being PLAYER.

clue.text: See 15
11, one who fiddled, given one 25 to get under way

indicators.note: in a down clue to get under means these pieces sit below the first word

parts.note: taken as written
Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned
taken as written
25 refers to 25-across, YEAR, abbreviated Y

explanation.surface: A player who fiddled is given one year to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: Emperor NERO 'fiddled while Rome burned'. 25 points to 25-across, YEAR, whose abbreviation is Y. The answer is the England footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: The England striker is a player in the sporting sense, 11-across being PLAYER.

clue.text: Leave under rocks, so hidden

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leave something under rocks so nobody finds it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like stones to hide things under, but it is the anagram signal for LEAVE UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrevealed means not disclosed, kept hidden, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Endlessly long time

indicators.note: Endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: Something going on forever, a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long time' reads as one phrase, but 'long' is wordplay (YEARN, less its end) and 'time' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time, the definition by example.

clue.text: Want to drop teacher into river

indicators.note: to drop into says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: Wishing to throw the schoolmaster in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests falling, but here it means putting one word into another; British pupils address a male teacher as 'sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and desire are synonyms, both meaning to wish for.

clue.text: The current Frenchman wants to 'inder English

parts.note: to hinder is to hamper; spoken with the H dropped it becomes 'amper

explanation.surface: A present-day Frenchman, in a Cockney accent, gets in the way of the English.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'inder shows the H dropped, so HAMPER loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampère was the French physicist, and the ampere is the unit of electric current named after him.
